{"parentUuid":"70dd4d79-ea9a-4472-a1e3-c63213770ec3","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"8fee48cb-92eb-4861-8f18-16792cc3cb95","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Tx8gwyU4b5KV2BVSsBoReC","type":"tool_result","content":"=== README\n# Kenyon Model UN Recaps CMS\n\nA content management system where club members write trip recaps and officers publish them to a static GitHub Pages site. It is IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2.\n\n## Features\n\n- Login with argon2 password hashes and CSRF protection on every form\n- Two roles, Admin and Editor, with Editors limited to their own Recaps\n- Trips and Recaps, with Draft, Submitted and Published states\n- Pages that appear in the public navigation\n- A dashboard with counts and a filterable content list\n- A Markdown editor with a sanitized Preview\n- Image uploads with required alt text\n- Account management, including Deactivate\n- `cms publish`, `cms deploy` and `cms backup` commands\n\n## Live URL\n\n- Site: <https://andrew-vera26.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/>\n- Repository: <https://github.com/andrew-vera26/iphs400-mp2-cms>\n\n## Run locally\n\nEvery command runs from the repository root, because `CMS_DATABASE` and\n`CMS_UPLOADS` are relative paths, and goes through `uv run --env-file .env` so\nthe settings in `.env` are loaded.\n\n1. Clone and install:\n\n   ```bash\n   git clone https://github.com/andrew-vera26/iphs400-mp2-cms.git\n   cd iphs400-mp2-cms\n   uv sync\n   ```\n\n2. Create `.env` from the template, then edit it and set `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD`\n   and `CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD` (and a long random `CMS_SECRET_KEY`). Keep values\n   with spaces in double quotes. `.env` is gitignored.\n\n   ```bash\n   cp .env.example .env\n   ```\n\n3. Seed the demo Admin and Editor accounts, a Trip, Recaps in every status and\n   two Pages. It is safe to run again.\n\n   ```bash\n   uv run --env-file .env python scripts/seed_demo.py\n   ```\n\n4. Start the admin console and open <http://localhost:8000/login>. Log in as\n   `admin@example.test` or `editor@example.test` with the passwords from `.env`.\n\n   ```bash\n   uv run --env-file .env cms serve\n   ```\n\n5. Render the published content into `site/` (generated; never edit it by hand).\n   Preview it with `python3 -m http.server -d site 8001`.\n\n   ```bash\n   uv run --env-file .env cms publish\n   ```\n\n6. Back up the database and uploaded images into a folder **outside** the\n   repository (the command refuses a folder inside it):\n\n   ```bash\n   uv run --env-file .env cms backup ~/cms-backups\n   ```\n\n7. Push `site/` to the `gh-pages` branch, then in the repository's Settings ->\n   Pages choose **Deploy from a branch**, `gh-pages`, `/ (root)`:\n\n   ```bash\n   uv run --env-file .env cms deploy\n   ```\n\n## What is here\n\n```text\napp/               the FastAPI admin console and the publisher\n  routes/          login, console, trips, recaps, pages and accounts routes\n  static/          admin.css, the admin stylesheet\ntemplates/         Jinja templates: admin/ (console) and public/ (published site)\ntests/             one test file per ticket (T00-T09), plus the admin style and 403 page tests\nscripts/           seed_demo.py, usage_report.py, check_submission.py\ndocs/              screenshots, handoffs, process notes and the project report\ndocs/adr/          three decision records (ADR-001 to ADR-003)\n.claude/hooks/     the context meter and usage ledger\nCONTEXT.md         the project glossary\n```\n\nThe CMS is complete (tickets T00-T09), both exercise functions, `decide()` and `spend()`, are implemented, the test suite passes, and the demo site is published to GitHub Pages from the `gh-pages` branch.\n\nRun `uv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 2` before you submit.\n\n## Backends used\n\n| Backend | Models | Phases | Swaps |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Anthropic API | Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 | All phases | None |\n\n## Generative AI Use Statement\n\nI built this project with Claude Code, following the grill, spec, tickets, and per-ticket workflow from the course manual. I used Claude Opus 5.5 for the grilling, spec, and ticket breakdown, and Claude Sonnet 5.5 at medium effort for implementing and reviewing each ticket. The skills I ran were grill-with-docs, to-spec, to-tickets, implement, tdd, code-review, and handoff. I also ran research subagents to look up WordPress functions for my field notes, and used /clear and /compact to manage context. The grill decisions were mine, including reversing the model's admins-only account design so Editors can log in at club meetings, and the rule that Editors see only their own Recaps.\n\nTwo prompts I used:\n1. \"Write the new tests first and run them. Show me the red run, then STOP and wait for me to say go before you write any implementation code.\"\n2. \"Stop. Answer these before doing anything else, with no changes to files. (1) Did you write tests/test_t05.py before any implementation code? (2) Did you run them and see them fail before implementing, and where in this session can I see that?\"\n\nOne real failure: on the first ticket the model implemented before showing a failing test, even though the workflow requires it. I caught it by asking directly whether it had run the tests red first, and it admitted it had not. After that I asked for the red run explicitly on every ticket. On T05 my prompt asked to show the red run but did not say to stop, so the model showed it and kept going, and I added an explicit stop to every later prompt.\n=== token plan\n# Token budget plan\n\n| Stage | Model | Effort | Estimate (% of a 5-hour window) |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Quick lookups | Haiku 5.5 | low | 1% |\n| /grill-with-docs | Opus 5.5 | high | 8% |\n| /to-spec | Opus 5.5 | high | 5% |\n| /to-tickets | Opus 5.5 | high | 5% |\n| /implement + /tdd (per ticket) | Sonnet 5.5 | medium | 5% |\n| /code-review (per ticket) | Sonnet 5.5 | high | 3% |\n\n**How many 5-hour windows will the 9 tickets take?** Planning is about 18%. The tickets are 9 x 8% = 72%. That's about 90% of one window, so I'm planning on two to leave room for rework.\n\n**How much of one week is that?** My status line showed 24% of a 5-hour window and 6% of the week, so one full window is roughly 25% of a week. Two windows is about half a week.\n\n**Which stage will I cut first if I'm wrong?** The stretch features (comments, uploads), then I'd drop /code-review from high to medium effort.\n(Part 5.4 of the manual. Fill this in before your first /implement.)\n=== ledger\nts,session,phase,provider,model,effort,ctx_pct,five_h_pct,weekly_pct\r\n2026-09-29T17:37:31Z,c73d83ab,unlabelled,anthropic,Fable It is IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2.\n\n## Features\n\n- Login with argon2 password hashes and CSRF protection on every form\n- Two roles, Admin and Editor, with Editors limited to their own Recaps\n- Trips and Recaps, with Draft, Submitted and Published states\n- Pages that appear in the public navigation\n- A dashboard with counts and a filterable content list\n- A Markdown editor with a sanitized Preview\n- Image uploads with required alt text\n- Account management, including Deactivate\n- `cms publish`, `cms deploy` and `cms backup` commands\n\n## Live URL\n\n- Site: <https://andrew-vera26.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/>\n- Repository: <https://github.com/andrew-vera26/iphs400-mp2-cms>\n\n## Run locally\n\nEvery command runs from the repository root, because `CMS_DATABASE` and\n`CMS_UPLOADS` are relative paths, and goes through `uv run --env-file .env` so\nthe settings in `.env` are loaded.\n\n1. Clone and install:\n\n   ```bash\n   git clone https://github.com/andrew-vera26/iphs400-mp2-cms.git\n   cd iphs400-mp2-cms\n   uv sync\n   ```\n\n2. Create `.env` from the template, then edit it and set `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD`\n   and `CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD` (and a long random `CMS_SECRET_KEY`). Keep values\n   with spaces in double quotes. `.env` is gitignored.\n\n   ```bash\n   cp .env.example .env\n   ```\n\n3. Seed the demo Admin and Editor accounts, a Trip, Recaps in every status and\n   two Pages. It is safe to run again.\n\n   ```bash\n   uv run --env-file .env python scripts/seed_demo.py\n   ```\n\n4. Start the admin console and open <http://localhost:8000/login>. Log in as\n   `admin@example.test` or `editor@example.test` with the passwords from `.env`.\n\n   ```bash\n   uv run --env-file .env cms serve\n   ```\n\n5. Render the published content into `site/` (generated; never edit it by hand).\n   Preview it with `python3 -m http.server -d site 8001`.\n\n   ```bash\n   uv run --env-file .env cms publish\n   ```\n\n6. Back up the database and uploaded images into a folder **outside** the\n   repository (the command refuses a folder inside it):\n\n   ```bash\n   uv run --env-file .env cms backup ~/cms-backups\n   ```\n\n7. Push `site/` to the `gh-pages` branch, then in the repository's Settings ->\n   Pages choose **Deploy from a branch**, `gh-pages`, `/ (root)`:\n\n   ```bash\n   uv run --env-file .env cms deploy\n   ```\n\n## What is here\n\n```text\napp/               the FastAPI admin console and the publisher\n  routes/          login, console, trips, recaps, pages and accounts routes\n  static/          admin.css, the admin stylesheet\ntemplates/         Jinja templates: admin/ (console) and public/ (published site)\ntests/             one test file per ticket (T00-T09), plus the admin style and 403 page tests\nscripts/           seed_demo.py, usage_report.py, check_submission.py\ndocs/              screenshots, handoffs, process notes and the project report\ndocs/adr/          three decision records (ADR-001 to ADR-003)\n.claude/hooks/     the context meter and usage ledger\nCONTEXT.md         the project glossary\n```\n\nThe CMS is complete (tickets T00-T09), both exercise functions, `decide()` and `spend()`, are implemented, the test suite passes, and the demo site is published to GitHub Pages from the `gh-pages` branch.\n\nRun `uv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 2` before you submit.\n\n## Backends used\n\n| Backend | Models | Phases | Swaps |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Anthropic API | Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 | All phases | None |\n\n## Generative AI Use Statement\n\nI built this project with Claude Code, following the grill, spec, tickets, and per-ticket workflow from the course manual. I used Claude Opus 5.5 for the grilling, spec, and ticket breakdown, and Claude Sonnet 5.5 at medium effort for implementing and reviewing each ticket. The skills I ran were grill-with-docs, to-spec, to-tickets, implement, tdd, code-review, and handoff. I also ran research subagents to look up WordPress functions for my field notes, and used /clear and /compact to manage context. The grill decisions were mine, including reversing the model's admins-only account design so Editors can log in at club meetings, and the rule that Editors see only their own Recaps.\n\nTwo prompts I used:\n1. \"Write the new tests first and run them. Show me the red run, then STOP and wait for me to say go before you write any implementation code.\"\n2. \"Stop. Answer these before doing anything else, with no changes to files. (1) Did you write tests/test_t05.py before any implementation code? (2) Did you run them and see them fail before implementing, and where in this session can I see that?\"\n\nOne real failure: on the first ticket the model implemented before showing a failing test, even though the workflow requires it. I caught it by asking directly whether it had run the tests red first, and it admitted it had not. After that I asked for the red run explicitly on every ticket. On T05 my prompt asked to show the red run but did not say to stop, so the model showed it and kept going, and I added an explicit stop to every later prompt.\n=== token plan\n# Token budget plan\n\n| Stage | Model | Effort | Estimate (% of a 5-hour window) |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Quick lookups | Haiku 5.5 | low | 1% |\n| /grill-with-docs | Opus 5.5 | high | 8% |\n| /to-spec | Opus 5.5 | high | 5% |\n| /to-tickets | Opus 5.5 | high | 5% |\n| /implement + /tdd (per ticket) | Sonnet 5.5 | medium | 5% |\n| /code-review (per ticket) | Sonnet 5.5 | high | 3% |\n\n**How many 5-hour windows will the 9 tickets take?** Planning is about 18%. The tickets are 9 x 8% = 72%. That's about 90% of one window, so I'm planning on two to leave room for rework.\n\n**How much of one week is that?** My status line showed 24% of a 5-hour window and 6% of the week, so one full window is roughly 25% of a week. Two windows is about half a week.\n\n**Which stage will I cut first if I'm wrong?** The stretch features (comments, uploads), then I'd drop /code-review from high to medium effort.\n(Part 5.4 of the manual. {"parentUuid":"18b0ed05-3a21-4982-b330-7d95bdbc5847","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"8fee48cb-92eb-4861-8f18-16792cc3cb95","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01FaCk8VA8HMLAQpkzq5EWcT","type":"tool_result","content":"=== REPORT\n# IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2: Kenyon Model UN Recaps CMS\n\nAndrew Vera · 24 October 2026 · Repo: https://github.com/andrew-vera26/iphs400-mp2-cms · Live site: https://andrew-vera26.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\n\n## 1. What I built, and which grill decisions were mine\n\nI built a content management system for the Kenyon Model UN club. Members write trip recaps in a FastAPI and SQLite console, officers publish them, and `cms publish` followed by `cms deploy` renders a static site to GitHub Pages. Recaps move from Draft to Submitted to Published, and the suite has 531 tests. The full feature list is in the README.\n\nThree grill decisions were mine. The model's first design let only Admins log in, which would have meant chasing the President across campus to enter every recap. I reversed it. Editors now log in on the President's laptop at Sunday meetings, and I recorded that in ADR-003. I also set the permission rule that Editors see and change only their own Recaps while Admins alone publish, and I ruled out Account reactivation and email password reset.\n\n## 2. Where the AI drifted, and what caught it\n\nThe clearest drift was on T04, the Markdown sanitizer. The spec says it strips all raw HTML. The model's first version escaped it instead, so `<script>` and `onerror=` survived as visible text, and three of my tests failed. It proposed loosening them to fit. I caught it by reading the failing tests against the spec instead of against the model's explanation. I made it restore the original assertions and fix the code, and the final version drops every raw-HTML token.\n\nTwo other things surfaced. On T01 the model wrote implementation before showing a failing test, and I only found out by asking it directly. Later, `/code-review`, which compares the diff to the spec, found that an Editor's save could land after an Admin had Published the Recap (fixed with a status-guarded UPDATE), and that `cms backup` of a missing database wrote an empty archive.\n\nThe bug I remember best is a small one. `.env.example` had an unquoted `CMS_SITE_TITLE` containing spaces. `uv run --env-file` couldn't parse that line and silently dropped every variable after it, so the seed script exited asking for `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD`. My tests had passed the values through the environment and never ran the documented command, so they never saw it. Running that command against a fresh clone did.\n\n## 3. Skills, prompts, and resources\n\nI followed the course workflow: `/grill-with-docs`, `/to-spec`, and `/to-tickets` on Opus 5.5, then nine tickets on Sonnet 5.5 at medium effort. Each ticket ran the same loop: `/clear`, `/implement` with `/tdd` (tests red before any code), `/code-review` in a fresh subagent, the findings posted on the GitHub issue, then a closing commit that names every file. I also used research subagents for the WordPress field notes, `/clear` between tickets, one manual `/compact`, and one handoff. I kept tickets small enough for one fresh session, which cost me some setup time per ticket but meant the model never worked from a stale, crowded context.\n\n## 4. What I would add next, and what the budget showed\n\n| Stage | Plan | Actual (% of a 5-hour window) |\n|---|---|---|\n| Planning (grill, spec, tickets) | 18% | 16% |\n| Tickets T01–T09 (implement, test, review) | 72% | 69% |\n| Final polish (admin stylesheet, 403 page, screenshots, README, deploy) | not planned | 12% |\n\nThe plan held: tickets averaged 7.7% against 8% planned, with T03 the most expensive at 13% and T05 the cheapest at 3%. What I missed was work outside the tickets. The final polish cost 12%, more than any ticket except T03, and 59% of the meter was logged as \"unlabelled\" because I started labelling phases late. A line for polish and an earlier habit of labelling would have made the plan honest.\n\nThe thing I'd change is how I wrote the ground rules. On T02 through T05 I asked the model to \"show me them failing before any implementation.\" It treated that as a report, not a gate. On T05 it showed a real red run (14 failed, 2 passed), implemented, and reached `/code-review` before I'd had a chance to look. The work was fine, but I could only check it after the fact. From T06 on, every prompt named stops: after the red run, after green, and before review. Next time the stops go in the first prompt.\n\nNext I would add a Deploy button in the console (it is terminal-only now), account reactivation, and a styled 404 for the public site. At about 8% per ticket, three tickets fit in one window. Debt I left: status transitions wired in five places, test files that import each other's helpers, and an image check that reads magic bytes without decoding.\n\n## Note on the submission check\n\n`check_submission.py` reports a failure for root-absolute paths in eleven console templates (`templates/admin/` and the console's base template). Those links (`/admin/...`) are correct because the console is served from the root and never published. The rubric rules (S1.7, F2, T6) concern the published site, where the tests and a grep over the rendered `site/` find none. I left the script unchanged and explain the failure here instead.","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"3dde84b9-0da9-44f3-b8c8-e7f490ab7e80","timestamp":"2026-10-24T20:17:15.384Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"=== REPORT\n# IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2: Kenyon Model UN Recaps CMS\n\nAndrew Vera · 24 October 2026 · Repo: https://github.com/andrew-vera26/iphs400-mp2-cms · Live site: https://andrew-vera26.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\n\n## 1. {"parentUuid":"c6c602f0-d7b2-4d0c-9451-d8223e7312fe","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"8fee48cb-92eb-4861-8f18-16792cc3cb95","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01KZHEgyYbg2g3izjvQ2MKVB","type":"tool_result","content":"{'unlabelled': 59.0, 'grill': 8.0, 'spec': 5.0, 'tickets': 4.0, 'T01': 7.0, 'T02': 7.0, 'T03': 14.0, 'T04': 11.0, 'T05': 6.0, 'T06': 9.0, 'T07': 11.0, 'T08': 10.0, 'T09': 12.0, 'FINAL': 17.0} 180.0\nT01 7.0\nT02 7.0\nT03 14.0\nT04 11.0\nT05 6.0\nT06 9.0\nT07 11.0\nT08 10.0\nT09 12.0\n# Kenyon Model UN Recaps\n\nA content system where the Kenyon Model UN club's officers publish recaps of the club's conference trips for the Kenyon community.\n\n## Content\n\n**Trip**:\nOne conference journey the club made, such as the Chicago conference. A Trip carries its own required Summary of what the trip was, and groups the Recaps written about it. A Trip appears on the Public site only once it has at least one Published Recap, and it can be deleted only while it has no Recaps.\n_Avoid_: Event, conference (as the record's name)\n\n**Summary**:\nAn Admin-written overview on a Trip: the conference, where it was, and what happened overall. Readers see it at the top of the Trip's page.\n_Avoid_: Description, intro\n\n**Recap**:\nOne club member's personal account of exactly one Trip. A Recap has a title, a Slug, a Markdown body with optional Images, a Byline, an Owner, and records of when it was created, last edited, and Published. It is written by an Editor, or entered by an Admin for a Contributor. Recaps are individual anecdotes, while the Trip's Summary says what the trip was. A Trip can have several Recaps.\n_Avoid_: Post, blog, article\n\n**Slug**:\nThe short, URL-safe name that identifies a Trip, Recap, or Page in the public site's addresses, such as `2026-chicago` or `chicago-food-crawl`. A Trip's Slug is unique among Trips, a Recap's within its Trip, and a Page's among Pages. A Page cannot take a Slug the site already uses, such as `trips` or `images`.\n_Avoid_: Permalink, path, handle\n\n**Byline**:\nThe writer's name and class year shown on a Recap, such as \"by Jane Doe '27\". Both parts are required. An Editor's or Admin's Byline comes from their Account, and an Admin types a Contributor's Byline by hand. A Page has a title, a Slug, a text-only Markdown body, a Draft or Published status, an Owner, and records of when it was created and last edited. Only Admins create, edit, or delete Pages.\n_Avoid_: Static page, post\n\n**Body**:\nThe Markdown text of a Recap or Page. IMPORTANT: These instructions OVERRIDE any default behavior and you MUST follow them exactly as written.\\n\\nContents of /Users/andrewv/.claude/CLAUDE.md (user's private global instructions for all projects):\\n\\n# CLAUDE.md\\n\\nThis file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.\\n\\n@~/Developer/browser-harness/SKILL.md\\n\\n# gstack\\n\\nUse the /browse skill from gstack for all web browsing. Never use mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.\\n\\nAvailable gstack skills: /office-hours, /plan-ceo-review, /plan-eng-review, /plan-design-review, /design-consultation, /design-shotgun, /design-html, /review, /ship, /land-and-deploy, /canary, /benchmark, /browse, /connect-chrome, /qa, /qa-only, /design-review, /setup-browser-cookies, /setup-deploy, /setup-gbrain, /retro, /investigate, /document-release, /codex, /cso, /autoplan, /plan-devex-review, /devex-review, /careful, /freeze, /guard, /unfreeze, /gstack-upgrade, /learn.\\n\\n@RTK.md\\n\\nContents of /Users/andrewv/Developer/browser-harness/SKILL.md (user's private global instructions for all projects):\\n\\n# browser-harness\\n\\nDirect browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py` and `agent-workspace/domain-skills/`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read install.md.\\n\\n## Usage\\n\\n```bash\\nbrowser-harness -c '\\nnew_tab(\\\"https://docs.browser-use.com\\\")\\nwait_for_load()\\nprint(page_info())\\n'\\n```\\n\\n- Invoke as browser-harness — it's on $PATH. No cd, no uv run.\\n- First navigation is new_tab(url), not goto_url(url) — goto runs in the user's active tab and clobbers their work.\\n\\nAvailable interaction skills:\\n- interaction-skills/connection.md — startup sequence, tab visibility, omnibox popup fix\\n\\nAvailable domain skills:\\n- tiktok/upload.md\\n- polymarket/scraping.md\\n\\n## Tool call shape\\n\\n```bash\\nbrowser-harness -c '\\n# any python. helpers pre-imported. daemon auto-starts.\\n'\\n```\\n\\nrun.py calls ensure_daemon() before exec — you never start/stop manually unless you want to.\\n\\n### Remote browsers\\n\\nUse remote for parallel sub-agents (each gets its own isolated browser via a distinct BU_NAME) or on a headless server. BROWSER_USE_API_KEY must be set. start_remote_daemon, list_cloud_profiles, list_local_profiles, sync_local_profile are pre-imported.\\n\\n```bash\\nbrowser-harness -c '\\nstart_remote_daemon(\\\"work\\\")                               # default — clean browser, no profile\\n# start_remote_daemon(\\\"work\\\", profileName=\\\"my-work\\\")      # reuse a cloud profile (already logged in)\\n# start_remote_daemon(\\\"work\\\", profileId=\\\"<uuid>\\\")         # same, but by UUID\\n# start_remote_daemon(\\\"work\\\", proxyCountryCode=\\\"de\\\", timeout=120)   # DE proxy, 2-hour timeout\\n# start_remote_daemon(\\\"work\\\", proxyCountryCode=None)      # disable the Browser Use proxy\\n'\\n\\nBU_NAME=work browser-harness -c '\\nnew_tab(\\\"https://example.com\\\")\\nprint(page_info())\\n'\\n```\\n\\nstart_remote_daemon prints liveUrl and auto-opens it in the local browser (if a GUI is detected) so the user can watch along. Headless servers print only — share the URL with the user. The daemon PATCHes the cloud browser to stop on shutdown, which persists profile state. Running remote daemons bill until timeout.\\n\\nProfiles (cookies-only login state) live in interaction-skills/profile-sync.md — covers list_cloud_profiles(), the chat-driven \\\"which profile?\\\" pattern, and sync_local_profile() for uploading a local Chrome profile.\\n\\n## Search first\\n\\nSearch `agent-workspace/domain-skills/` first for the domain you are working on before inventing a new approach.\\n\\nOnly if you start struggling with a specific mechanic while navigating, look in interaction-skills/ for helpers. The available interaction skills are:\\n- cookies.md\\n- cross-origin-iframes.md\\n- dialogs.md\\n- downloads.md\\n- drag-and-drop.md\\n- dropdowns.md\\n- iframes.md\\n- network-requests.md\\n- print-as-pdf.md\\n- profile-sync.md\\n- screenshots.md\\n- scrolling.md\\n- shadow-dom.md\\n- tabs.md\\n- uploads.md\\n- viewport.md\\n\\nUseful commands:\\n\\n```bash\\nrg --files agent-workspace/domain-skills\\nrg -n \\\"tiktok|upload\\\" agent-workspace/domain-skills\\n```\\n\\n## Always contribute back\\n\\nIf you learned anything non-obvious about how a site works, open a PR to `agent-workspace/domain-skills/<site>/` before you finish. Default to contributing. The harness gets better only because agents file what they learn. If figuring something out cost you a few steps, the next run should not pay the same tax.\\n\\nExamples of what's worth a PR:\\n\\n- A private API the page calls (XHR/fetch endpoint, request shape, auth) — often 10× faster than DOM scraping.\\n- A stable selector that beats the obvious one, or an obfuscated CSS-module class to avoid.\\n- A framework quirk — \\\"the dropdown is a React combobox that only commits on Escape\\\", \\\"this Vue list only renders rows inside its own scroll container, so scrollIntoView on the row doesn't work — you have to scroll the container\\\".\\n- A URL pattern — direct route, required query params (?lang=en, ?th=1), a variant that skips a loader.\\n- A wait that wait_for_load() misses, with the reason.\\n- A trap — stale drafts, legacy IDs that now return null, unicode quirks, beforeunload dialogs, CAPTCHA surfaces.\\n\\n### What a domain skill should capture\\n\\nThe *durable* shape of the site — the map, not the diary. Focus on what the next agent on this site needs to know before it starts:\\n\\n- URL patterns and query params.\\n- Private APIs and their payload shape.\\n- Stable selectors (data-*, aria-*, role, semantic classes).\\n- Site structure — containers, items per page, framework, where state lives.\\n- Framework/interaction quirks unique to this site.\\n- Waits and the reasons they're needed.\\n- Traps and the selectors that *don't* work.\\n\\n### Do not write\\n\\n- Raw pixel coordinates. They break on viewport, zoom, and layout changes. Describe how to *locate* the target (selector, scrollIntoView, aria-label, visible text) — never where it happened to be on your screen.\\n- Run narration or step-by-step of the specific task you just did.\\n- Secrets, cookies, session tokens, user-specific state. `agent-workspace/domain-skills/` is shared and public.\\n\\n## What actually works\\n\\n- Screenshots first: use capture_screenshot() to understand the current page quickly, find visible targets, and decide whether you need a click, a selector, or more navigation.\\n- Clicking: capture_screenshot() → read the pixel off the image → click_at_xy(x, y) → capture_screenshot() to verify. Suppress the Playwright-habit reflex of \\\"locate first, then click\\\" — no getBoundingClientRect, no selector hunt. Drop to DOM only when the target has no visible geometry (hidden input, 0×0 node). Hit-testing happens in Chrome's browser process, so clicks go through iframes / shadow DOM / cross-origin without extra work.\\n- Bulk HTTP: http_get(url) + ThreadPoolExecutor. No browser for static pages (249 Netflix pages in 2.8s).\\n- After goto: wait_for_load().\\n- Wrong/stale tab: ensure_real_tab(). Use it when the current tab is stale or internal; the daemon also auto-recovers from stale sessions on the next call.\\n- Verification: print(page_info()) is the simplest \\\"is this alive?\\\" check, but screenshots are the default way to verify whether a visible action actually worked.\\n- DOM reads: use js(...) for inspection and extraction when the screenshot shows that coordinates are the wrong tool.\\n- Iframe sites (Azure blades, Salesforce): click_at_xy(x, y) passes through; only drop to iframe DOM work when coordinate clicks are the wrong tool.\\n- Auth wall: redirected to login → stop and ask the user. Don't type credentials from screenshots.\\n- Raw CDP for anything helpers don't cover: cdp(\\\"Domain.method\\\", params).\\n\\n## Design constraints\\n\\n- Coordinate clicks default. Input.dispatchMouseEvent goes through iframes/shadow/cross-origin at the compositor level.\\n- Connect to the user's running Chrome. Don't launch your own browser.\\n- cdp-use is only for CDPClient.send_raw. Prefer raw CDP strings over typed wrappers.\\n- run.py stays tiny. No argparse, subcommands, or extra control layer.\\n- Core helpers stay short. Put task-specific helper additions in `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`; daemon/bootstrap and remote session admin live in the core package.\\n- Don't add a manager layer. No retries framework, session manager, daemon supervisor, config system, or logging framework.\\n\\n## Gotchas (field-tested)\\n\\n- Omnibox popups are fake page targets. Filter chrome://omnibox-popup... and other internals when you need a real tab.\\n- CDP target order != Chrome's visible tab-strip order. Use UI automation when the user means \\\"the first/second tab I can see\\\"; Target.activateTarget only shows a known target.\\n- Default daemon sessions can go stale. ensure_real_tab() re-attaches to a real page.\\n- Browser Use API is camelCase on the wire. cdpUrl, proxyCountryCode, etc.\\n- Remote cdpUrl is HTTPS, not ws. Resolve the websocket URL via /json/version.\\n- Stop cloud browsers with PATCH /browsers/{id} + {\\\"action\\\":\\\"stop\\\"}.\\n- After every meaningful action, re-screenshot before assuming it worked. Use the image to verify changed state, open menus, navigation, visible errors, and whether the page is in the state you expected.\\n- Use screenshots to drive exploration. They are often the fastest way to find the next click target, notice hidden blockers, and decide if a selector is even worth writing.\\n- Prefer compositor-level actions over framework hacks. Try screenshots, coordinate clicks, and raw key input before adding DOM-specific workarounds.\\n- If you need framework-specific DOM tricks, check interaction-skills/ first. That is where dropdown, dialog, iframe, shadow DOM, and form-specific guidance belongs.\\n\\n## Interaction notes\\n\\n- interaction-skills/ holds reusable UI mechanics such as dialogs, tabs, dropdowns, iframes, and uploads.\\n- `agent-workspace/domain-skills/` holds site-specific workflows and should be updated when you discover reusable patterns for a website.\\n\\nContents of /Users/andrewv/.claude/RTK.md (user's private global instructions for all projects):\\n\\n# Command output\\n\\nCommand output here is condensed to save tokens, keeping every signal and\\ndropping costly noise. Add a rule only after you have had to correct the same thing\\ntwice.\\n\\n## What this repo is\\n\\nA small web CMS for IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2. A local admin console\\n(FastAPI + Jinja + SQLite) writes content; `cms publish` renders the published\\ncontent into `site/` as static HTML, which is deployed to GitHub Pages. The\\nadmin console never goes on the public internet.\\n\\n## Hard constraints\\n\\n- Published HTML uses **relative** paths only. Never `href=\\\"/...\\\"` or `src=\\\"/...\\\"`.\\n- Never commit `.env`, `*.db`, keys, or tokens. Read secrets from the environment.\\n- Passwords are hashed with argon2. Never store or log a plain password.\\n- Every state-changing form carries a CSRF token.\\n- User-written Markdown is sanitized before it is rendered anywhere.\\n- `site/` is generated. Never edit it by hand.\\n- Only published content reaches `site/`. Drafts never leave the database.\\n\\n## How to work with me\\n\\n- One ticket per session. Read the ticket issue, the spec issue, and `CONTEXT.md`\\n  before writing code.\\n- Write the ticket id into `.claude/state/phase` when a stage starts\\n  (`grill`, `spec`, `tickets`, or `T03`), so the usage ledger is labelled.\\n- Use the vocabulary in `CONTEXT.md`. Then commit with a message that\\n  starts `T0N:` and ends `Closes #N`.\\n- Ask before adding a dependency. The stack in `pyproject.toml` is fixed for this\\n  project.\\n\\n## Long sessions (shared standard)\\n- Session handoffs are dated, write-once files in `docs/handoffs/`, named `<YYYY-MM-DD_HHMM>_<slug>-claude.md`: `/handoff <slug>` writes one, `/handoff-load <slug>` loads one by name. `LATEST*.md` and `INDEX.md` are retired stubs (2026-10-06): never read, write or import them. Codex keeps its own records in `docs/handoffs/codex/`.\\n- Compaction snapshots and the automatic compaction record come from the global `compact_snapshot.py` hook (global CLAUDE.md, \\\"Long runs\\\" and \\\"Compaction\\\"); this repository has no handoff hooks of its own.\\n- Session exports (`/export` files, `codex-session-*.md`) and other files that appear in this repository from another session, agent, directory or machine are the owner's work, never foreign. Exports live in `transcripts/` (move a stray one there), are scanned by the git hooks, and are included in every commit; `bin/repo-standardize` in `~/code/ai-swe-setup` does the move.\\n- Decisions and gotchas discovered in conversation go into the handoff or an ADR under `docs/adr/`, never only in chat.\\n- When compacting, preserve: the goal, the ordered next steps, every decision with its reason, the modified files and their state, the exact test and lint commands with their last results, and the open questions. Drop raw tool output and resolved detours.\\n## Agent skills\\n\\n### Issue tracker\\nGitHub Issues via the `gh` CLI (PRs are not a triage surface). IMPORTANT: These instructions OVERRIDE any default behavior and you MUST follow them exactly as written.\\n\\nContents of /Users/andrewv/.claude/CLAUDE.md (user's private global instructions for all projects):\\n\\n# CLAUDE.md\\n\\nThis file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.\\n\\n@~/Developer/browser-harness/SKILL.md\\n\\n# gstack\\n\\nUse the /browse skill from gstack for all web browsing. Never use mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.\\n\\nAvailable gstack skills: /office-hours, /plan-ceo-review, /plan-eng-review, /plan-design-review, /design-consultation, /design-shotgun, /design-html, /review, /ship, /land-and-deploy, /canary, /benchmark, /browse, /connect-chrome, /qa, /qa-only, /design-review, /setup-browser-cookies, /setup-deploy, /setup-gbrain, /retro, /investigate, /document-release, /codex, /cso, /autoplan, /plan-devex-review, /devex-review, /careful, /freeze, /guard, /unfreeze, /gstack-upgrade, /learn.\\n\\n@RTK.md\\n\\nContents of /Users/andrewv/Developer/browser-harness/SKILL.md (user's private global instructions for all projects):\\n\\n# browser-harness\\n\\nDirect browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py` and `agent-workspace/domain-skills/`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read install.md.\\n\\n## Usage\\n\\n```bash\\nbrowser-harness -c '\\nnew_tab(\\\"https://docs.browser-use.com\\\")\\nwait_for_load()\\nprint(page_info())\\n'\\n```\\n\\n- Invoke as browser-harness — it's on $PATH. No cd, no uv run.\\n- First navigation is new_tab(url), not goto_url(url) — goto runs in the user's active tab and clobbers their work.\\n\\nAvailable interaction skills:\\n- interaction-skills/connection.md — startup sequence, tab visibility, omnibox popup fix\\n\\nAvailable domain skills:\\n- tiktok/upload.md\\n- polymarket/scraping.md\\n\\n## Tool call shape\\n\\n```bash\\nbrowser-harness -c '\\n# any python. helpers pre-imported. daemon auto-starts.\\n'\\n```\\n\\nrun.py calls ensure_daemon() before exec — you never start/stop manually unless you want to.\\n\\n### Remote browsers\\n\\nUse remote for parallel sub-agents (each gets its own isolated browser via a distinct BU_NAME) or on a headless server. BROWSER_USE_API_KEY must be set. start_remote_daemon, list_cloud_profiles, list_local_profiles, sync_local_profile are pre-imported.\\n\\n```bash\\nbrowser-harness -c '\\nstart_remote_daemon(\\\"work\\\")                               # default — clean browser, no profile\\n# start_remote_daemon(\\\"work\\\", profileName=\\\"my-work\\\")      # reuse a cloud profile (already logged in)\\n# start_remote_daemon(\\\"work\\\", profileId=\\\"<uuid>\\\")         # same, but by UUID\\n# start_remote_daemon(\\\"work\\\", proxyCountryCode=\\\"de\\\", timeout=120)   # DE proxy, 2-hour timeout\\n# start_remote_daemon(\\\"work\\\", proxyCountryCode=None)      # disable the Browser Use proxy\\n'\\n\\nBU_NAME=work browser-harness -c '\\nnew_tab(\\\"https://example.com\\\")\\nprint(page_info())\\n'\\n```\\n\\nstart_remote_daemon prints liveUrl and auto-opens it in the local browser (if a GUI is detected) so the user can watch along. Headless servers print only — share the URL with the user. The daemon PATCHes the cloud browser to stop on shutdown, which persists profile state. Running remote daemons bill until timeout.\\n\\nProfiles (cookies-only login state) live in interaction-skills/profile-sync.md — covers list_cloud_profiles(), the chat-driven \\\"which profile?\\\" pattern, and sync_local_profile() for uploading a local Chrome profile.\\n\\n## Search first\\n\\nSearch `agent-workspace/domain-skills/` first for the domain you are working on before inventing a new approach.\\n\\nOnly if you start struggling with a specific mechanic while navigating, look in interaction-skills/ for helpers. The available interaction skills are:\\n- cookies.md\\n- cross-origin-iframes.md\\n- dialogs.md\\n- downloads.md\\n- drag-and-drop.md\\n- dropdowns.md\\n- iframes.md\\n- network-requests.md\\n- print-as-pdf.md\\n- profile-sync.md\\n- screenshots.md\\n- scrolling.md\\n- shadow-dom.md\\n- tabs.md\\n- uploads.md\\n- viewport.md\\n\\nUseful commands:\\n\\n```bash\\nrg --files agent-workspace/domain-skills\\nrg -n \\\"tiktok|upload\\\" agent-workspace/domain-skills\\n```\\n\\n## Always contribute back\\n\\nIf you learned anything non-obvious about how a site works, open a PR to `agent-workspace/domain-skills/<site>/` before you finish. Default to contributing. The harness gets better only because agents file what they learn. If figuring something out cost you a few steps, the next run should not pay the same tax.\\n\\nExamples of what's worth a PR:\\n\\n- A private API the page calls (XHR/fetch endpoint, request shape, auth) — often 10× faster than DOM scraping.\\n- A stable selector that beats the obvious one, or an obfuscated CSS-module class to avoid.\\n- A framework quirk — \\\"the dropdown is a React combobox that only commits on Escape\\\", \\\"this Vue list only renders rows inside its own scroll container, so scrollIntoView on the row doesn't work — you have to scroll the container\\\".\\n- A URL pattern — direct route, required query params (?lang=en, ?th=1), a variant that skips a loader.\\n- A wait that wait_for_load() misses, with the reason.\\n- A trap — stale drafts, legacy IDs that now return null, unicode quirks, beforeunload dialogs, CAPTCHA surfaces.\\n\\n### What a domain skill should capture\\n\\nThe *durable* shape of the site — the map, not the diary. Focus on what the next agent on this site needs to know before it starts:\\n\\n- URL patterns and query params.\\n- Private APIs and their payload shape.\\n- Stable selectors (data-*, aria-*, role, semantic classes).\\n- Site structure — containers, items per page, framework, where state lives.\\n- Framework/interaction quirks unique to this site.\\n- Waits and the reasons they're needed.\\n- Traps and the selectors that *don't* work.\\n\\n### Do not write\\n\\n- Raw pixel coordinates. They break on viewport, zoom, and layout changes. Describe how to *locate* the target (selector, scrollIntoView, aria-label, visible text) — never where it happened to be on your screen.\\n- Run narration or step-by-step of the specific task you just did.\\n- Secrets, cookies, session tokens, user-specific state. `agent-workspace/domain-skills/` is shared and public.\\n\\n## What actually works\\n\\n- Screenshots first: use capture_screenshot() to understand the current page quickly, find visible targets, and decide whether you need a click, a selector, or more navigation.\\n- Clicking: capture_screenshot() → read the pixel off the image → click_at_xy(x, y) → capture_screenshot() to verify. Suppress the Playwright-habit reflex of \\\"locate first, then click\\\" — no getBoundingClientRect, no selector hunt. Drop to DOM only when the target has no visible geometry (hidden input, 0×0 node). Hit-testing happens in Chrome's browser process, so clicks go through iframes / shadow DOM / cross-origin without extra work.\\n- Bulk HTTP: http_get(url) + ThreadPoolExecutor. No browser for static pages (249 Netflix pages in 2.8s).\\n- After goto: wait_for_load().\\n- Wrong/stale tab: ensure_real_tab(). Use it when the current tab is stale or internal; the daemon also auto-recovers from stale sessions on the next call.\\n- Verification: print(page_info()) is the simplest \\\"is this alive?\\\" check, but screenshots are the default way to verify whether a visible action actually worked.\\n- DOM reads: use js(...) for inspection and extraction when the screenshot shows that coordinates are the wrong tool.\\n- Iframe sites (Azure blades, Salesforce): click_at_xy(x, y) passes through; only drop to iframe DOM work when coordinate clicks are the wrong tool.\\n- Auth wall: redirected to login → stop and ask the user. Don't type credentials from screenshots.\\n- Raw CDP for anything helpers don't cover: cdp(\\\"Domain.method\\\", params).\\n\\n## Design constraints\\n\\n- Coordinate clicks default. Input.dispatchMouseEvent goes through iframes/shadow/cross-origin at the compositor level.\\n- Connect to the user's running Chrome. Don't launch your own browser.\\n- cdp-use is only for CDPClient.send_raw. Prefer raw CDP strings over typed wrappers.\\n- run.py stays tiny. No argparse, subcommands, or extra control layer.\\n- Core helpers stay short. Put task-specific helper additions in `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`; daemon/bootstrap and remote session admin live in the core package.\\n- Don't add a manager layer. No retries framework, session manager, daemon supervisor, config system, or logging framework.\\n\\n## Gotchas (field-tested)\\n\\n- Omnibox popups are fake page targets. Filter chrome://omnibox-popup... and other internals when you need a real tab.\\n- CDP target order != Chrome's visible tab-strip order. Use UI automation when the user means \\\"the first/second tab I can see\\\"; Target.activateTarget only shows a known target.\\n- Default daemon sessions can go stale. ensure_real_tab() re-attaches to a real page.\\n- Browser Use API is camelCase on the wire. cdpUrl, proxyCountryCode, etc.\\n- Remote cdpUrl is HTTPS, not ws. Resolve the websocket URL via /json/version.\\n- Stop cloud browsers with PATCH /browsers/{id} + {\\\"action\\\":\\\"stop\\\"}.\\n- After every meaningful action, re-screenshot before assuming it worked. Use the image to verify changed state, open menus, navigation, visible errors, and whether the page is in the state you expected.\\n- Use screenshots to drive exploration. They are often the fastest way to find the next click target, notice hidden blockers, and decide if a selector is even worth writing.\\n- Prefer compositor-level actions over framework hacks. Try screenshots, coordinate clicks, and raw key input before adding DOM-specific workarounds.\\n- If you need framework-specific DOM tricks, check interaction-skills/ first. That is where dropdown, dialog, iframe, shadow DOM, and form-specific guidance belongs.\\n\\n## Interaction notes\\n\\n- interaction-skills/ holds reusable UI mechanics such as dialogs, tabs, dropdowns, iframes, and uploads.\\n- `agent-workspace/domain-skills/` holds site-specific workflows and should be updated when you discover reusable patterns for a website.\\n\\nContents of /Users/andrewv/.claude/RTK.md (user's private global instructions for all projects):\\n\\n# Command output\\n\\nCommand output here is condensed to save tokens, keeping every signal and\\ndropping costly noise. Add a rule only after you have had to correct the same thing\\ntwice.\\n\\n## What this repo is\\n\\nA small web CMS for IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2. A local admin console\\n(FastAPI + Jinja + SQLite) writes content; `cms publish` renders the published\\ncontent into `site/` as static HTML, which is deployed to GitHub Pages. The\\nadmin console never goes on the public internet.\\n\\n## Hard constraints\\n\\n- Published HTML uses **relative** paths only. Never `href=\\\"/...\\\"` or `src=\\\"/...\\\"`.\\n- Never commit `.env`, `*.db`, keys, or tokens. Read secrets from the environment.\\n- Passwords are hashed with argon2. Never store or log a plain password.\\n- Every state-changing form carries a CSRF token.\\n- User-written Markdown is sanitized before it is rendered anywhere.\\n- `site/` is generated. Never edit it by hand.\\n- Only published content reaches `site/`. Drafts never leave the database.\\n\\n## How to work with me\\n\\n- One ticket per session. {"parentUuid":"25d0086a-849d-41be-ac3b-987f93609c58","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"8fee48cb-92eb-4861-8f18-16792cc3cb95","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Pp6UbgMaxnAmDAqqsbjQQd","type":"tool_result","content":"=== client brief\n# Client brief: Kenyon Model United Nations\n\n## Who runs the site\nThe club's officers run it: the President and the Vice President. These two are the sole admins. They are moderately comfortable with computers, perhaps being college students speaks for itself. Club members write the recaps of each trip, and editors with their own logins can publish their own posts, while only the admins manage users and everything else.\n\n## Who reads it\nThe Kenyon community. They come to remain updated on how the Model United Nations competitions go for the team: where the team traveled, how the competition was, whether it was competitive, whether they explored the new place, whether they tried any new foods. Ultimately it's just detailing their travels. The club travels once or twice a semester, most recently to Chicago, so posts are infrequent and each one matters.\n\n## What is broken now\nThe club doesn't have an official site. It uses Instagram to publicize any club activities, so recaps get buried in a feed and nobody can look back at a past trip.\n\n## What would make them say \"this is better\"\nAn active website with accessible blogs that include pictures and anecdotes would be a much better alternative to Instagram. If possible, they'd also like a comment section, but that's a nice-to-have, not a requirement.\n\n## What must not happen\nNobody except approved editors can edit the blogs. An editor must never be able to create users, change roles, or edit another person's recap.=== field notes\n# Field notes\n\n(Part 2 of the manual: at least five things you noticed inside WordPress Playground, in your own words.)\n# CMS field notes (WordPress Playground)\n\n- When I created a new user with the Editor role and logged in as them, I could no longer get to Settings. WordPress's docs say editors can manage content but can't change site settings or add new users, so this matches. [Add what happened when you tried Users: was the menu gone, or did you get an error message?]\n- The first post I wrote went under \"My WordPress Website,\" the default site name. After that I made my own site, which shows in the top right as \"Kenyon Political Science.\" [Add one sentence on whether that was confusing.]\n- I like the \"All Posts\" tab. It's intuitive and lists everything I've posted so far, and it has links at the top to filter by status, like Published or Draft.\n- Every URL was built the same way, and they all had \"WordPress\" in them. The part that comes from the post's title is called the slug. [Add one real example URL from Settings → Permalinks.]\n- I expected to see my post on the public site as soon as I saved it, but I couldn't until I published it. Saving a draft keeps it private.=== commit bodies\n--- 4fa0815 Add submission README and Stage 2 report\nFiles: README.md, docs/iphs400_mp2-web-cms_report_andrew-vera_20261024.md,
